ekegusii: abanto 55 gotooka nebinyinyi bia Corona, ewizara yobochenu yatebire Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 25, 2022 Abanto 55 nigo baenegetigwe nebinyinyi bia Corona maega yabanto 1934 korengwa ase chinsa 24 chiaetete. Koreng’ana newizara yobochenu, 45 ase abwo nabakenya ase 10 bare abamaiko. 36 nabasacha na 19 nabasubati, omoke pi nonmwana bwemika 2, ase omogotu pi abwate emiaka 88. Ekaonty ya Nairobi eyatang’anete nabanto 39, Uasin Gishu 6, ekaonty ya Murang’a 4,Busia 2, Mombasa2, Kiambu amo na Kisumu oyomo oyomo. Omowaziri bwobochenu Mutahi Kagwe natebete abanto 153 babwenire korwa ase endwari eyio, ase 152 babwena ase chinka noyomo korwa ase enyagitari. Ase bono abanto 53 nigo batangire ase chinyagitari ao ao kobwatekana nendwari eyio ase abande 797 bagendererete konyora obogwenia korwa ase chiinka. Ase bono, morwaire taiyo ore ICU, onde taiyo obekeire mbeo na onde taiyo ore HDU.
english: Abanto 55 experienced several deaths due to Corona, the Ministry of Health has confirmed. Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 25, 2022 Abanto 55 is among those who died from Corona, bringing the total to 1934 since March 24th. According to the Ministry of Health, 45 were men and 10 were women. 36 were over the age of 60 and 19 were under the age of 30, including a two-year-old child and an 88-year-old man. Nairobi County recorded 39 cases, Uasin Gishu 6, Murang’a County 4, Busia 2, Mombasa 2, Kiambu and Kisumu each had one case. Minister of Health Mutahi Kagwe reported that 153 people tested positive for the disease, while 152 recovered from the illness. Also, 53 people are currently admitted to intensive care units, 797 are isolated at home with mild symptoms, and another 797 are awaiting test results. Furthermore, there are patients in general wards, some requiring oxygen support and others in High Dependency Units.

ekegusii: Omoruoti bw'semi abwenererete gochora omorai orache magega yaye ekero akure. Omoruoti naareganeti ekeragerio ekenene mono na eng'ana nere atagete kobamanyia. Ase igo bakagende chinsanganio chiosi chiorosana. Ekero omotienyi omesete, Omoruoti Engo agacha na gotenena gatigati yabo. Ching'iti chiosi chigakira kiri na gotegerera omoruoti akuane. Kegoteba, "Karwoa nchira ng'ete. Ninche omonene bwenererete koba eruoti." Ritimo rikagwa inse kobara goika kane. Enchogu ekaigwa obororo egachaka gotinera amagoro inse. Omoruoti Engo akamotebia, "Nkwarenge neribaga riago." Aseigo Enchogu ekagenda. Ebeche egacha kegoteba, "Karwa nchera yane. Karwa nchera yane. Niche kochia koba omoruoti. ninche bwate ekeonwa ekenene. Ninche omokong'u. Nibwenererete koba omoruoti." Ritimo rikagwa inse goika kobara isanonemo. Ekaigwa obororo. Ekabea na koeruta ebuse embeo igoro. Engo ekamotebia, "Beche okoruta nigo kware rimo rioka. Ribaga riao riaerire." Ebeche ekagenda. Chinsa echio bakaigwa eriogi korwa magega yabo. Ekero barigereretie magega bagaichana keria baroche. Egana ekaira ritimo ekarisira gochia igoro. Ekang'usa okoboko gochia igoro, ekaminyoka gochia bosio, egacharoka igoro, ekaruta ritimo gochia rire igoro. "Rimo! Kabere! Gatato! Kane! Gatano! Gatanorimo! Gatanokabere! Obee!" Egana ekarera. Egana ekabea. Ekaigwa obororo ekang'ea goonchokanana, gekoemurukania na gotamereria amang'ana amange. Korende Omoruoti Engo akamotebia, "Yaya, nigo okonyora ribaga erimo rioka." Ase igo Egana ekagenda. Ekero ching'iti chinde chiaigwete amang'ana aye, chionsi chigachaka goseka. Ekaeyana, ekabuatoka ritimo egatuora, "Gatano omente gatano ni ikomi." Ritimo rikagwa inse. Omoruoti Engo atateba, "Eee, Engabi! Isano omente isano neenchera yogoika ikomi. Chichera nechinyinge chiokobara goika ikomi." Erwarenerero tiyarenge yokonyora eng'iti enene gose eyebuate chinguru kobua echinde. Erwano eyarenge yokonyora eng'iti eng'aini kobua chionsi. Naboigo Engabi yabete Enting'ana ekero Engo yakwete. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0 Source www.africanstorybook.org
english: The girl who speaks well can attract a husband and have many children. The girl does not reveal her beauty completely, only showing enough to make him desire her. Thus they spend their days in endless teasing. When a young man approaches, Omoruoti Engo hides and carefully observes him. Every day she finds a way to protect herself from the boy. She says, “Marry me quickly. I am beautiful and worthy of being married.” Time passes and he tries to find a way to approach her. The herd of cattle grazes peacefully, unaware of his intentions. Omoruoti Engo reflects, “I will wait for the right time.” And so the herd moves on. The calf cries out, “Marry me now. Marry me now. Let me be close to the girl. I am strong and capable. I am worthy of the girl.” Time passes and he continues to try to approach her. The herd grazes peacefully. The ground trembles with the weight of countless hooves. Engo reflects, “Let the calf continue to chase until time reveals itself. The right time will come.” The calf moves on. This story tells of a boy approaching a herd of cattle. They guard themselves closely, separating those who seek to harm them. The dawn arrives, bringing with it a new rhythm to the land. The sun rises, illuminating the hills, the valleys, the plains, and the riverbanks. “Time! Friend! Enemy! Now! Five! Six! Seven! Eight!” Dawn proclaims. The dawn awakens. The herd scatters, running in different directions, shaking and trembling with fear. Then Omoruoti Engo reflects, “Yes, this is how time reveals itself.” And so dawn departs. Every small thing that falls upon the earth is covered in dust. Everything shakes and settles. The wind whispers a rhythm, saying, “Five times five is twenty-five.” Time passes. Omoruoti Engo says, “Yes, Engabi! Twenty times twenty is four hundred. This secret will reveal itself.” Tradition dictates that one should not reveal a large tree to someone who wants to cut it down. It also dictates that one should not reveal a small plant to anyone. But today, Engabi met Enting'ana, and Engo saw. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0 Source www.africanstorybook.org

ekegusii: Nyasae nigo agosaria emeroberio y’abang’ainereria, erinde emeremo bagokora namaboko abo tegoikerana buna baganetie.
english: He thwarts the plans of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.

ekegusii: Omochiki oria bw’abarendi akaira Yeremia ensemo, akamotebia, “Omonene, Nyasae oo, nararetie ng’a amang’ana aya amabe nayenyore ense eye.
english: When the commander of the guard found Jeremiah, he said to him, "The LORD your God decreed this disaster for this place.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’amang’ana ayio kaerire Ibrahimu agatebigwa ng’a, “Milka oiboreire momura omino Nahori abana.
english: Some time later Abraham was told, "Milcah is also a mother; she has borne sons to your brother Nahor:

ekegusii: Obobe koborachiche igoro asetore, gose esegi, gose egesusuro, gose oborwaire bogoita, gose enchara, natotenene bosio bw’enyomba eye ase obosio bwao, ekiagera erieta riao nao rire ase enyomba eye. Igo ntonyare korera asore ase engencho y’emechando yaito, aye noigwe ototoorie.
english: 'If calamity comes upon us, whether the sword of judgment, or plague or famine, we will stand in your presence before this temple that bears your Name and will cry out to you in our distress, and you will hear us and save us.'

ekegusii: Naki Nyasae tatomete Omwana oye ase ense agambie ense, korende ense etoorigwe nere.
english: For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him.

ekegusii: “Amang’ana aya naro batotebia: Intwe nigo tore abasomba ba Nyasae o igoro na ense, na nigo tokoagacha naende enyomba eria omoruoti omonene bw’Abaisraeli aagachete na akayekoora ase emiaka emenge yaetire.
english: This is the answer they gave us: "We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago, one that a great king of Israel built and finished.

ekegusii: Omonene akaba nendamwamu enene ase Abaisraeli, na ekero ase ekero akaba okobabeka ase okoboko kwa Hasaeli, omoruoti bw’Abasiiria, na ase okwa Beni‐Hadadi, mosinto o Hasaeli.
english: So the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and for a long time he kept them under the power of Hazael king of Aram and Ben-Hadad his son.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, ere oyobwangire aya, tangeti mwanyabanto, korende Nyasae, oyokobaa inwe Omoika oye Omochenu.
english: Therefore, he who rejects this instruction does not reject man but God, who gives you his Holy Spirit.

ekegusii: Oyo noro omobaro bwe chiamate chi’Abagerisoni, abarigetwe, abwo baare konyara gokora emeremo ase Eema y’Omosangererekano, abwo Musa na Haroni babarete, buna Omonene achigete.
english: This was the total of those in the Gershonite clans who served at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the LORD's command.

ekegusii: Nong’oonerie endagera indie na amache inywe, nainche ninkoe chibesa. Aye ing’a ribaga ng’ete namagoro ase ense yao.
english: Sell us food to eat and water to drink for their price in silver. Only let us pass through on foot--

ekegusii: Ekero omoruoti aroche Esteri eting’ana oteneine ase egoora, Esteri akanyora ogwancherwa asare. Omoruoti akamworotera enyimbo yaye y’oboruoti eroisirie korwa ase etahabu, arenge nero koboko. Erio Esteri akagenda gochia ang’e, agakuna mesia y’enyimbo eria,
english: When he saw Queen Esther standing in the court, he was pleased with her and held out to her the gold scepter that was in his hand. So Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter.

ekegusii: Nigo morarue asebare, mwetwegete amaboko ase emetwe, ekiagera Omonene bwangire abanto abwo mosemeretie, rirorio timokonyora ogosesenigwa amo nabarabwo.”
english: You will also leave that place with your hands on your head, for the LORD has rejected those you trust; you will not be helped by them.

ekegusii: Boigo bakarua emegwekano eria ye chimbeba eroisirie korwa ase chitahabu, oyomo korwa ase kera omochie orenge kogamberwa nabanene baria batano b’Abafilisti, emechie eyio yonsi yagiteire chindwaki na ebichie bionsi bitagiteire. Ne rigena riria rinene ase babegete Esanduku eria y’Omonene nigo rire kirori goika rituko ria rero agwo ase omogondo o Yoshua o Beti‐Semesi.
english: And the number of the gold rats was according to the number of Philistine towns belonging to the five rulers-- the fortified towns with their country villages. The large rock, on which they set the ark of the LORD, is a witness to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.

ekegusii: Daudi akamoboria, “Noyo ng’o ore? Seino ng’ai?” Omosae oria akairaneria, “Inche nigo inde omomura bw’Abamisiri na omosomba bw’omonto oyomo Omoameleki. Bono amatuko atato aerire korwa ekero omonene one antigete, ekiagera nabete omorwaire.
english: David asked him, "To whom do you belong, and where do you come from?" He said, "I am an Egyptian, the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me when I became ill three days ago.

ekegusii: Korende Yeso akabarangeria bache asare, ogoteba, “Batige abana bache asende, timobaisa kobatanga, ekiagera abare buna aba, oboruotibwa Nyasae nobwabo.
english: But Jesus called the children to him and said, "Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

ekegusii: Ekero arandangerie, inche nimoitabere, inche nigo inde amo nere ase engaki y’emechando. Nimotoorie, naende nimoe ogosika.
english: He will call upon me, and I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble, I will deliver him and honor him.

ekegusii: Na barabwo bagachia goika ase Yeso, bakamosorora, bakabora, “Nagwenerete omokorere ring’ana eri,
english: When they came to Jesus, they pleaded earnestly with him, "This man deserves to have you do this,

ekegusii: Korende Farao agakong’ia enkoro yaye nonya nengaki eyio, taa abanto ribaga bagende.
english: But this time also Pharaoh hardened his heart and would not let the people go.

ekegusii: Yohana akairaneria, “Omonto takonyara konyora ring’ana rinde rionsi otatiga aegwe korwa igoro.
english: To this John replied, "A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.

ekegusii: Korende Yeroboamu, mosinto o Nebati, omosomba o Sulemani, mosinto o Daudi, akarega omonene oye omoruoti, akaanga komoigwera.
english: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, an official of Solomon son of David, rebelled against his master.

ekegusii: Nabarabwo bakaria na konywa ase obosio bw’Omonene ase rituko riria, bakaba nomogoko omonene. Bono eria kabere bakabeka Sulemani, mosinto o Daudi, akaba omoruoti obo; bakamoaka amaguta akaba omogambi ase ogokorera Omonene, na Zadoki agaakwa amaguta akaba omokuani.
english: They ate and drank with great joy in the presence of the LORD that day. Then they acknowledged Solomon son of David as king a second time, anointing him before the LORD to be ruler and Zadok to be priest.

ekegusii: “Aye Omonene, rigereria buna inde ase emechando, omoyo one oonchokanire, na enkoro yane yaonchoranirwe, ekiagera nabeire oyo otari omoigweri. Abana baane baitirwe nemioro ase chinchera, na amakweri abeire ase enka yane,
english: "See, O LORD, how distressed I am! I am in torment within, and in my heart I am disturbed, for I have been most rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is only death.

ekegusii: Amang’ana abanto abang’aini bagokwana nigo anga buna chimbambo chinyoge, na aya basangereirie anga buna emesumari eakeire bokong’u. Ayio onsi nebiegwa korwa ase Omorisia oyomo.
english: The words of the wise are like goads, their collected sayings like firmly embedded nails-- given by one Shepherd.

ekegusii: Nigo morabarigie abwo bakobasoera, ko timokobanyora; abwo barenge kobarwania nigo barabe bosa kegima.
english: Though you search for your enemies, you will not find them. Those who wage war against you will be as nothing at all.

ekegusii: Amo nabarabwo twatomire oyominto oyotwarorire ara aange ase amang’ana amange ng’a nare nomokia, na bono nare nomokia kobua, ekiagera ase ogosemeria are nakorokwo asemore.
english: In addition, we are sending with them our brother who has often proved to us in many ways that he is zealous, and now even more so because of his great confidence in you.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’engaki gete moka omonene oye akarigereria Yusufu ase okomogania, akamotebia, “Inchuo orare nainche!”
english: and after a while his master's wife took notice of Joseph and said, "Come to bed with me!"

ekegusii: Ekero ise biara Musa aroche onsi aya Musa are gokorera abanto, akamoboria. “Inki eke ogokorera abanto? Naki oikaransete aye bweka, na abanto bagoetanaine korwa mambia goika mogoroba?”
english: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you alone sit as judge, while all these people stand around you from morning till evening?"

ekegusii: “Ntwamoigwete ogoteba: Inche nintagore Hekalu eye yakoregete namaboko, na ase amatuko atato ning’agache eyende etakoregeti namaboko.”
english: "We heard him say, 'I will destroy this man-made temple and in three days will build another, not made by man.'"

ekegusii: Tokonye, torwanie ababisa baito tobabue, ekiagera ogokonywa gokorwa ase mwanyabanto mbosa.
english: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Amo na Joshua Araka: Gusii.com/2010, Manga Escarpment. Embeo nigo ekogusa korwa Enyancha ya Victoria yaaka Emanga. Nigo embeo egotengia emete ye emanga. Eye nero e Manga gose Manga Escarpment buna abande bakoyeroka. Emanga nigo ere ange chieka 100. Nigo ere ime ya Manga District ange na Kisii Town. Nigo E Manga ere ase orobebe rwa Kitutu Masaba na Kitutu Chache. Goteneine ase e Manga, nabo okorora Kisii Town, Bogere,Enyancha ya Victoria amo ne chinsemo chinde chia Nyamira District. Enyomba yo Omogusii nigo yarenge "round". Omosongo nere orentete chikona. Enyomba yaito Manga yaagachetwe ne Ritongo Cultural Group yagotire. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Abangina na abagaka abakoro ba Gusii nigo bagoteba inga E Manga nigo yarenge ase Abagusii barenge koumerana gosaba, gokora ebingwanso ne emeyega yende yonsi emenene. Omogaka Omondi Onkundi, 70, nigo agoteba inga abakoloni nigo baagachete Ekoti (Ritongo) entangani ime ya Gusii aaiga ase E Manga.Omogaka Onkundi nigo agoteba inga ekero omokoloni arwete Gusii, Ritongo rikanganyigwa gochia Nyamira. Gopreserve omogaino oito. Gotaka komanya ase twarwete. Ribwago Cultural Group. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Engoro No Omosasa O' Kegancha Nigo omogaka Onkundi agoteba inga, otatiga ogotamanyekana ase chingaki echi chie ekerero, E Manga nigo yasikire sana ase amatuko amakoro. Abagusii nigo beegenete inga chisokoro na Nyasae (Engoro) nao bameneyete igaa. Omogaka Onkundi nigo akomenta inga erieta "Nyasae" nigo twasumete korwa Bogere. Nyasae tiriri rieta rie Ekegusii asiri. Erieta rironge ase Omogusii ribaga ria Nyasae nigo rire "Engoro". Buna ebisaku binde, Abagusii nigo bare gosuma amarieta goeta goeta kobwatekana buna barenge goetanana ase okonganya. Omogaka Onkundi nigo agoteba inga engaki ya botuko, nabo emerero yare kororekana egwoka ase chinsana chie E Manga. Nigo abanto bare kogenda maambia korotota banyora inga kende tikeyieti. Omogaka Samuel Ongeri nigo agoteba inga ekio ne ekeene rakini nigo akomenta inga omoika bwe Engoro nigo omenyete ase omote okorokwa Omosasa O'Kegancha. Aaiga ase Omosasa O 'Kegancha nao Abagusii barenge gosaba ase Engoro na komoboria aramere ababisa, gosibia emechie na koyesesenia. "Goikera rero, Omosasa O'Kegancha nao oteneine ase E Manga. Onde takoyobutora gose atumie chinko chiaye. Echio ne chimuma." Nabo omogaka Ongeri amentete. Omosasa O' Kegancha. Oteneine korwa kare kare. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Ngoro Mwaga Tari igo rioka. Egento kende kere ase E Manga ne engoro ekorokwa "Ngoro Mwaga". Nigo engoro eye echakerete egetare igoro, egaeta gati na goika inse. Nigo gekoba inga engoro eye nigo ere eya amasikani ase Engoro. Onye gotagete goika ange, goika okore emeroberio gete erinde omanye koyerora. Engoro Ya Mwaga tegoichora. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 "Goika osibe obonyansi bore machani kabichi amo ne chinko. Basi omanye koruta obonyansi obwo amo ne chinko echio ase engoro eyio ime. Korwa abwo chisokoro nabo chikogwanchera origererie engoro eyio". Nabo omogaka Onkundi akomenta. Nonya nabo igo, engoro eyio tiyana goichora obonyansi ne chinko gesa na gesa. Abagusii nigo beegenete inga emioyo ye chisokoro nao yamenyete aaiga ase E Manga. Nigo bare gocha igaa korwa ebingwanso, gosaba na gokora emeyega ende yonsi emenene. Renta obonyansi ne chinko momanye korigereria Engoro Ya Mwaga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Enyancha Yo Okari Ange na Ngoro Mwaga, enyancha neroo etari kororekana ekorokwa Enyancha Yo Okari. Nigo Omogano Bwa Abagusii ogoteba inga omochie oyomo nomenyete igaa rakini enyomba yabo ekarimera gochia inse ne echancha ekamanya gotoka. Yaani enyomba eyio nigo yanywetwe ne enyancha. Enyancha eyio nigo erokire erieta rio omogaka bwe enka eyio yanywetwe, omogaka Okari. Igena Monto Ebinto bie E Manga ne ebinge. Eariganie koumera Igena Monto. Gati ye ebinto ebinge bie E Manga bire ne maana ase Omogusii ne rigena rikorokwa Igena Monto. Rigena eri nigo rikororekana buna omonto. Korwa aare, nigo rikororekana buna omonto oikaransete rakini ekero gwaikire ange, kwanyora inga ne rigena. Omogusii nigo anchete goaka oboche. Nigo togoteba igo ekiagera chingoro chio ogoakera oboche bwa Ajua nao chichongire ase egetare igoro ase E Manga. Nigo William Marianga and Andrew Okera bagoaka oboche rakini nigo batebete inga oboche obo nigo bwarosetigwe ne Engoro. Tari monto oboroisetie. Goaka oboche E Manga igoro. Aba imbamanyete go kill time! Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Abamenyi be E Manga nigo batagete ogobago robekwe, chioteli chibekwe amo ne Museum ebwate Omogano o Gusii ne ebinto Abagusii bagatwarire. Ase amatuko aetire, ekeombe kia NGO kie Ritongo Cultural Group ingiatagete koagacha enyomba ye egetamaduni, babeke abateri bo obokano na abangina na abagaka bagototebia omogano bwo Omogusii. Kende tikeraba goikera bono ase engencho yo oboremerwa bwe chibesa. Togende gotara E Manga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Abanene be Ritongo Cultural Group, Ezra Abuga Na George Morara nigo bagoteba inga enyomba yaagachetwe bono yagotire. Nigo enyomba eye yaagachire ase ekegambero kio omochifu omokoro, Zachary Angwenyi. Aaiga nao gekoba inga Omochifu Angwenyi nigo agambete na korwa ogochika kwo ogokeia enamba ye chiombe chie enyangi korwa 20 impaka 6! "Eke nakio kiagerete Abasacha abange ba Gusii bagaansa konywoma naende". Nabo Ezra abuga akomenta naende. Konyora abasacha abange batigire konywoma ase engencho yo ogotatwara chiombe 20 na gochia igoro. Gusii.com iyakorete obotuki na konyora inga eserikali iyatagete kobeka Manga Escarpment ebe e National Monument. Emepango eyio teraba. Nigo ensemo eye ere engiya ase obotari rakini tebwati batari bange. Ase okogamba no omowaziri bwe Egetamaduni naende omobunge o North Mugirango, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui, nigo egotebekana inga emeroberio neroo yo okorenda na koroisia E Manga. "Nigo E Manga ebwate ekieni sana naende nabo erarente amagenderero sana toise koyerenda". Nabo Mhe. Ombui amentete. Assistant Minister For National Heritage and MP, North Mugirango Borabu, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Nigo Mhe. Ombui atebete inga naborie eserikali erwe ogokonya erinde Manga Cultura Center eagachwe. Ase boigo, nigo atebete inga netakeire orobago robekwe erinde emepaka yaye emanyekane.
english: These are the stories: Amo and Joshua Araka: Gusii.com/2010, Manga Escarpment. Long ago there was a person called Enyancha of Victoria who lived in Emanga. It was a person who owned land in Emanga. And now it is in Manga near Manga Escarpment where people gather. Emanga is about 100 years old. It is located in Manga District and Kisii Town. In Manga it borders Kitutu Masaba and Kitutu Chache. It has connections to Manga, also reaching Kisii Town, Bogore, Victoria Falls and even some parts of Nyamira District. The homesteads of the Gusii people were usually “round”. The fences were very short. This Manga homestead was built by the Ritongo Cultural Group and is well known. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Together with the elders of the Gusii people they say that Manga is where the Gusii people used to meet for consultations, perform ceremonies and resolve all important matters. Elder Omondi Onkundi, 70, says that the colonialists found the Ritongo (Cultural Center) already established within the territory of the Gusii people specifically at Manga. Elder Onkundi says that when the colonialists came to Gusii, Ritongo was moved to Nyamira. Let us preserve our traditions. Let us remember our history. Ribwago Cultural Group. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The Wealth of the Clan of Kegancha Elder Onkundi says that it is not widely known that this area, Manga, was very significant to the ancestors. The Gusii people believed that their strength came from God (the Creator) and they respected tradition. Elder Onkundi comments that the name "God" was first heard in Bogore. God’s creation for the Gusii people is referred to as "Engoro". However, in ancient times, the Gusii people had many different ways of life but they always united to solve problems. Elder Onkundi says that because of tribal conflicts, things often deteriorated leading to chaos in Manga. People would travel far and wide spreading rumors causing anxiety. Elder Samuel Ongeri says that this place and its surroundings are sacred and he comments that the name Engoro originated from the ancestor Okorokwa Omosasa O'Kegancha. The clan of Omosasa O 'Kegancha and the Gusii people worshipped Engoro and offered sacrifices, performed rituals and sought blessings. “Therefore, Omosasa O'Kegancha and his descendants are in Manga. He did not move anywhere during his lifetime. This is his home and burial ground.” Also said elder Ongeri. Omosasa O' Kegancha. Descendants live everywhere. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The Name of the Year This year has passed. A celebration took place in Manga and the name given was “Ngoro Mwaga”. It was a unique name which attracted attention and caused excitement. It was agreed upon that this name represented the strength of Engoro. Anyone who understood its meaning knew how important it was to protect it. The Name of the Year is celebrated. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 “It is good to respect both the living and the dead. Therefore, let us protect this heritage both now and in the future so that this name continues to be remembered.” Also commented Elder Onkundi. However, this name does not celebrate the living and the dead equally. The Gusii people believe that their ancestors have power and they honor them in Manga. They offer gifts, worship and pray for prosperity and peace. Respect both the living and the dead to preserve the Name of the Year. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The Story of Okari Like Ngoro Mwaga, this story also happened in the past called the Story of Okari. It is said that the history of the Gusii people tells of a man named Oyomo who lived near a tree whose roots were deep and branches spread wide. That tree was associated with a story. This story is about what happened to the elder named Okari. A Certain Person There are things in Manga and elsewhere. Let us remember a certain person called Igena Monto. Both things from Manga and elsewhere have meaning to the Gusii people and are remembered as Igena Monto. This memory is about a person. In the past, it was about a person who was respected by everyone, and it is still remembered today. The Gusii people also have traditions. It is believed that there was a time when a young man named Ajua went looking for traditions in Manga. William Marianga and Andrew Okera also searched for traditions and found that those traditions were preserved by Engoro. There is much more to learn. Searching for Traditions in Manga. Sometimes we just want to pass the time! Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The elders of Manga have realized that something needs to be done, a building should be built and a museum established to showcase the culture of the Gusii people and the items they used. For generations, organizations like the Ritongo Cultural Group have worked hard to preserve our heritage, bringing together leaders, experts and elders to promote the culture of the Gusii people. We need to support them in this endeavor. Let's continue to develop Manga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Leaders of the Ritongo Cultural Group, Ezra Abuga and George Morara, have stated that the land allocated for this purpose is sufficient. It is land that belonged to a former leader, Zachary Angwenyi. People say that Chief Angwenyi gave permission for the construction of a house with twenty rooms and six bathrooms! “I urge all the clans of the Gusii people to come together.” Ezra said. They encourage the clans to contribute towards building twenty rooms and six bathrooms. Gusii.com reports that efforts are underway to persuade the government to declare Manga Escarpment a National Monument. These plans are progressing. And there is hope that future generations will benefit from this. According to the Minister for Culture and Member of Parliament for North Mugirango, Hon. Wilfred Ombui, he supports the idea of preserving and developing Manga. “Manga has a lot of history and it can attract tourists if developed properly,” Hon. Ombui added. Assistant Minister For National Heritage and MP, North Mugirango Borabu, Hon. Wilfred Ombui. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Hon. Ombui further stated that the government should help fund the construction of the Manga Cultural Center. Additionally, he mentioned that funds should be allocated to renovate the existing structures so that their importance is recognized.

ekegusii: Erio Abaisraeli bakarera ase Omonene ng’a abatoorie, nere akabaa omonto kobatooria. Omonto oria nere Ehudi, mosinto o Gera, bw’egesaku kia Benjamin. Ehudi nigo arenge omonyakebee. Abaisraeli bagatoma Ehudi koirera Egiloni, omoruoti bw’ense ya Moabu, ebiegwa bi’amasikani.
english: Again the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and he gave them a deliverer-- Ehud, a left-handed man, the son of Gera the Benjamite. The Israelites sent him with tribute to Eglon king of Moab.

ekegusii: Ben-Abinadab-- in Naphoth Dor (he was married to Taphath daughter of Solomon);
english: Beni‐Abinadab agatenenera Nafati‐Dori yonsi (nere onyuomete Tafati, omoiseke o Sulemani);

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakaamboka Yorodan rituko ria ikomi ri’omotienyi bwe ritang’ani, bagatoora Giligali, ase orobebe rwa moocha ya Yeriko.
english: On the tenth day of the first month the people went up from the Jordan and camped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho.

ekegusii: Nathani agatebia omoruoti, “Genda okore ande onsi ayare ase ebirengererio biao, ekiagera Omonene nigo are amo naye.”
english: Nathan replied to the king, "Whatever you have in mind, go ahead and do it, for the LORD is with you."

ekegusii: Aye nigo ore omochenu ase abwo bare abachenu; nigo okwanga abwo bare abakorekanu.
english: to the pure you show yourself pure, but to the crooked you show yourself shrewd.

ekegusii: Inche Omonene nindete emechando asore Arieli, okorera na okweumia mbibe ime yao, na aye omochie nobe asende Arieli bori.
english: Yet I will besiege Ariel; she will mourn and lament, she will be to me like an altar hearth.

ekegusii: Omoruoti agakorera Esteri omoyega omonene bw’amasikani, akarangeria abanene bonsi b’obogambi na abasomba baye aroro. Boigo akarareria abanto bakeanerigwe ebango ase ense yaye, naende akarua ebiegwa ebinge buna omoruoti agwenerete akore.
english: And the king gave a great banquet, Esther's banquet, for all his nobles and officials. He proclaimed a holiday throughout the provinces and distributed gifts with royal liberality.

ekegusii: “Ekero mwanaaririe omochie na koyoboera ase engaki entambe, na koyorwania esegi, erinde moyoire, timobaisa gosaria emete ereo. Monyare koria amatunda ’emete eyio, korende timoyegecha. Inee! Emete nero nabanto erinde moyesirie?
english: When you lay siege to a city for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees by putting an ax to them, because you can eat their fruit. Do not cut them down. Are the trees of the field people, that you should besiege them?

It is said that the people of Makairo heard about this event and were saddened. They gathered together and discussed it, saying, "Because I am afraid of being beaten." Everyone laughed at this, saying, "Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha! Because I am afraid of being beaten." And the people of Gusii always say that when someone speaks foolishly or makes empty promises, they are like Nyaribari, the wife of Mogeni. Flikr/Wonderlane The author and Edwin son of Okong’o, the child of eight, Mache Ng’umbu. People. Storytellers. Ancestors, children of the past. Remember this lesson well! Once upon a time, when the land was still new, the elder from Makairo, a man who understood the Gusii customs, went to Kebirigo to learn more about the Gusii traditions. Anyone who wants to know about our history should listen carefully to the stories told by our ancestors, or seek guidance. Anyone who wants to understand our culture should respect the wisdom of the elders and honor their teachings. It is important to remember that our ancestors faced many challenges, but they persevered through hard work and determination. That is the story of the elder who lived a long life, and how he taught his children and grandchildren to live in harmony with nature and with each other. The elder was known as Mogaka. Every evening, he would gather his family around the fire and share stories of the past. (This is a good example of how to teach children about their heritage.) Our ancestors worked tirelessly to ensure that future generations would inherit a rich cultural legacy, and we must continue to uphold those values. Siberia is cold, oh Siberia is cold, Mosaiga Ayeee, ayee Mosaiga Give me strength, Mosaiga give me strength to persevere Ayeee, ayee Mosaiga Our ancestors also say that Mogaka named his clan "Mong’ina". He then went to conquer Mong’ina. He did so with courage and determination. “Yes, my father, I will obey Bosire,” Mogaka declared. “Good!” “I will bring you the head of an enemy.” Mong’ina refused to accept this offer and instead chose to reconcile with his enemies and make peace. Therefore, let us remember, let us… The shield of the warrior, let us… “I will obey Bosire, but first,” Mogaka said thoughtfully. “Let me see what this shield can do.” “Nyakerario,” Mong’ina replied respectfully. “It has the power to protect us from harm and to guide us on our journey.” Everyone laughed until they were breathless. Mong’ina then became the leader of his people. Nyakerario skillfully crafted shields, and the elders cherished them greatly. They also remembered the day when the people of Mong’are gathered together to celebrate their victory, singing and dancing joyfully. “Yes, that Ratemo was very brave,” the elder from Nyambati remarked. “Yes, let him go,” everyone agreed. Mong’are and Ratemo set out on a mission to prove their worth. “My friends, let us pray,” Mogaka began. “What shall we offer to appease the spirits?” “Bring some honey,” Nyambati suggested. “And some tobacco, so that Momanyi may find ‘esagasaga’ and discover the secrets of the forest.” “Why does she ask for that?” the elder inquired curiously. “Because Momanyi is wise and knowledgeable. She knows how to interpret dreams and visions, and she can use her powers to help us overcome obstacles.” Everyone laughed again until they could laugh no more. “Yes, let us allow them to pass,” Nyambati concluded. “Let them go,” Mogaka agreed. “Yes, let Mochumbe go and bring back news of the outside world,” Mong’ina added. “Alright,” Mogaka conceded. “Let us send messengers. Mochumbe is skilled at gathering information and reporting accurately.” Mochumbe and his companions traveled far and wide, listening to the BBC Swahili Service. The elders decided that the people should accompany Nyakerario on a visit to the market. They went with gifts. Mogaka refused to sleep, staying awake all night to contemplate his thoughts. “This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity! This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity!” That is when the young boy was born. We know his name, "This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity." He grew up quickly, becoming strong and healthy like an American. First, he told stories about how Americans had destroyed everything with weapons. To make a prosperous home, one needs a cow, a goat, and a hen. The land was fertile and abundant, providing plenty of food. And because of this abundance, people were able to raise children and prosper. But this story is just beginning. A prosperous home, a beautiful garden, and a television set where people gather to watch. The American way of life has spread throughout Kenya, bringing both benefits and challenges. Meat is expensive, but American meat is readily available. Remember that Ondieki once lamented the loss of traditional foods, saying that they were healthier and more satisfying. But the American way of life, the American dream, is being promoted through special programs and events. We continue onward, people of Gusii, remembering our traditions. Americans are now involved in politics, claiming that they can bring progress and development. These politicians often use empty promises and lies to deceive people, causing confusion and chaos. The consequences of their actions are felt by everyone, especially the poor and vulnerable. I remember hearing someone say, “What will happen next? Will this dream ever come true?” Many years later, my mother, Nyaituga, passed away. She left behind a legacy of strength and resilience. Americans' obsession with wealth prevents them from finding happiness. They accumulate possessions and money endlessly. I heard that an American spent $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) to bury his pet. When a pet dies, they perform a ritual called "Putting it to sleep" - they take the animal to a special place. It is said that there is a place called Pet Cemetery, where Americans bury their pets, along with their toys and belongings. They then grieve and mourn, comparing their grief to losing a child. This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity. --end of article-- Edwin Okongo is a researcher and writer from Gusii.com.
