These elders also decided to visit Osoro to understand the situation of the elders' meeting, and the people there complained that they had not been informed properly. These elders also gathered together after being summoned due to the accident involving a boda-boda rider, and they went to see his motorcycle, and this issue was discussed extensively, and the meeting ended with a resolution to support the family of the deceased and provide them with assistance from the Gusii community fund. They requested the committee members to cooperate with them during the investigation and to ensure that this meeting is successful and that the agenda is achieved.

ekegusii: “Ogokora kwabo kwabatangire tibairanera Nyasae obo. Omoika bw’obotomani nigo ore ime yabo, tibamomanyeti Omonene.
english: "Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God. A spirit of prostitution is in their heart; they do not acknowledge the LORD.

ekegusii: Bworokie enchera ase omoro oraetere, eyemo gochia ase Raba ase ense y’Abaamoni, na eyende ase Yerusalemu, omochie ogiteire chindwaki, ase ense y’Abayuda.
english: Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites and another against Judah and fortified Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Nimbatome gochia korwania egesaku ekio giasaririe ase Nyasae, ee, nimbachike bagende korwania abanto abwo nabeire nendamwamu asebare, mbasakore ebinto bi’abanto abwo bibe ebiabo, naende mbabatiringere inse buna esike ere ase chinchera.
english: I send him against a godless nation, I dispatch him against a people who anger me, to seize loot and snatch plunder, and to trample them down like mud in the streets.

ekegusii: akabatebia, “Mwandeterete omonto oyo, buna oyobaonchoire abanto; naunirie amang’ana aye ase amasio aino, na tindochi bobe ase omonto oyo ase aria mwamosoerete,
english: and said to them, "You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined him in your presence and have found no basis for your charges against him.

ekegusii: nor thieves nor the greedy nor drunkards nor slanderers nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
english: gose abaibi, gose abegimeria, gose abagotinda, gose abarami, gose abauri.

ekegusii: Ee, nigo akoebereretie, agakorusia korwa ase chimbanderana, agakorenta aase aagare, ase komigwa gotaiyo; boigo chindagera kwabekeretwe emesa nigo chiarenge chinoru.
english: "He is wooing you from the jaws of distress to a spacious place free from restriction, to the comfort of your table laden with choice food.

ekegusii: Omoisraeli oyomo agacha akarentana omokungu oyomo bw’Abamidiani ase eamate yaye, ase obosio bwa Musa amo nomoganda bwonsi kobateneine agwo ase egesoero ki’Eema y’Omosangererekano, bakorera.
english: Then an Israelite man brought to his family a Midianite woman right before the eyes of Moses and the whole assembly of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

ekegusii: What advantage, then, is there in being a Jew, or what value is there in circumcision?
english: Gaki rende, Omoyahudi inki abuete abande? Na okwaroka inki kogwenerete?

ekegusii: “Na bono, inwe abana baane, ntegerere moigwe, mbasesenirie abwo barendete chinchera chiane,
english: "Now then, my sons, listen to me; blessed are those who keep my ways.

ekegusii: Ebing’wanso ebio amo nokoruegwa okwo goika mobirue ase Omonene ase chingaki chi’Amatuko aino Amanene achorire. Nabirobio bimentwe ase ebing’wanso biaino mwariete chiira ng’a morue, na ebing’wanso bi’ogwancha, onye nebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa, gose okoruegwa kw’endagera, gose okw’ebinyugwa, gose ebing’wanso bi’omorembe.
english: "'In addition to what you vow and your freewill offerings, prepare these for the LORD at your appointed feasts: your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings and fellowship offerings. '"

ekegusii: “Aragererigwe omonto okorina omomenyi, gose entakana, gose omoboraka, oboronge bwaye. Abanto bonsi bairanerie, batebe: Amina.
english: "Cursed is the man who withholds justice from the alien, the fatherless or the widow." Then all the people shall say, "Amen!"

ekegusii: Ase ayio, nebe ekero Omonene, Nyasae oino, abaeire ense eria ebe omwando oino, naende ekero abaeire obotoereru korwa ase ababisa baino bonsi babaetanaine, goika mosirie Abaameleki bonsi, tibainyorwa nonya ng’ake inse y’erioba. Timobaisa kweba amang’ana ayio.
english: When the LORD your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!

ekegusii: Nyuma y’ayio Abisalomu akenyorera egari, ne chibarasi, na abanto emerongo etano barabe bakominyoka bosio bwaye.
english: In the course of time, Absalom provided himself with a chariot and horses and with fifty men to run ahead of him.

ekegusii: Okoirana nyuma kw’abwo batamanyeti amange nkobaite, na ogoisaneka kw’abariri nkobasirie barabwo abanyene.
english: For the waywardness of the simple will kill them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them;

ekegusii: ekiagera arenge kworokereria aborokigwa baye, akabatebia ng’a, “Omwana‐o‐mwanyabanto nkogenda are kobekwa ase amaboko ’abanto, na barabwo nabamoite, na ekero aitirwe naboke nyuma y’amatuko atato.”
english: because he was teaching his disciples. He said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be betrayed into the hands of men. They will kill him, and after three days he will rise."

ekegusii: Ase engencho y’emechando y’abanto baane enkoro yane yachandekire. Nigo nkorera na kweumia, ekiagera naichoirwe nomoondoko.
english: Since my people are crushed, I am crushed; I mourn, and horror grips me.

ekegusii: Ase ensemo ya sugusu y’Obomenyo oroisie chibao emerongo ebere,
english: For the other side, the north side of the tabernacle, make twenty frames

ekegusii: Oboriri nigo bore omogoko ase omonto otabwati okomanya, korende omonto omong’aini nigo akobwatia chinchera chi’oboronge.
english: Folly delights a man who lacks judgment, but a man of understanding keeps a straight course.

ekegusii: Erio Serubabeli, mosinto o Sealitieli, na Yesua, mosinto o Yosadaki, bagachaka koagacha naende enyomba ya Nyasae agwo Yerusalemu, na ababani ba Nyasae mbarengeo amo nabarabwo ase okobakonya.
english: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak set to work to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem. And the prophets of God were with them, helping them.

ekegusii: Nigo nkona‐koong’anya inde nemechando ntarochi omobaso; nigo ngotenena ase omosangererekano, narera ng’a nkonywe.
english: I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

ekegusii: Omoruoti agatebia Amasa, “Rangeria Abayuda bache asende ekero amatuko atato ataraera; naye obe aiga ase engaki eyio.”
english: Then the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself."

ekegusii: Eting’ana ya Irianyi netenene ase rituko ri’ekina amo nabanto b’ekegori eke; ere nabanachere ekina, ekiagera nigo arwete ase chinsinyo chi’ense anyare koigwa obong’aini bwa Sulemani; na rora, oyobuete Sulemani naiga are.
english: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom, and now one greater than Solomon is here.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, inwe abanto b’ebisaku, na inwe omoganda bwonsi, tegerera moigwe amang’ana agochia kobanyora abwo bangire.
english: Therefore hear, O nations; observe, O witnesses, what will happen to them.

ekegusii: Akamoboria eria kabere, “Simion mosinto o Yohana, nonyanchete?” Akamoiraneria, “Ee, Omonene, aye nomanyete ng’a ningwanchete.” Akamotebia, “Risia ching’ondi chiane.”
english: Again Jesus said, "Simon son of John, do you truly love me?" He answered, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Take care of my sheep."

english: You will overthrow every fortified city and every major town. You will cut down every good tree, stop up all the springs, and ruin every good field with stones."

ekegusii: Rhapidophyllum hystrix Rhapidophyllum hystrix n’eyemo ye Chipamu chikoremerereia obokendu obonene ase chimbego chie chipamu. Embego n’eyemo yoka ere ase egesaku kia Rhapidophyllum. Igoogosimekwa ase akendu ase chinsemo chia USA ya maate- moino. Korene n’gesio ase okoremeriria kwaye kw’obokendu bore inse buna chidigiri 20 igo yaanchire monoe getich mono imeya Yuropu. Nigo ere embego y’epamu enkong’u, naende ekwama chimita 1–3 chioka ase obotambe n’amagwa amaya ase ritina. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix igo ere enke ekorusia chimbande raisi, amatina amange akorosia ekemeri ekegare mono. Ase engaki entambe, amatina ayio narosi orosana oronene. Epamu y’esindani teri korosi matina korende ekobi erakine goika chimita 1,2 ase obotambe goika 17,8 ase obogare. Amatina nigo abwate amato amakoro, amatwaro, n’amagwa amatanyerere amatambe. Nigo atirete buya , gose aarare inse ekiagere chikorwanerera oborabu gose ekiriri. Chintetere nigo chigosimekwa ase abwate amache. Ase amiaka 3 ametang’ani. Nigo etakeire chibe are n’obokendu. Epamu y’esindani igo egotaka ase are n’omoika bwa amache naende ebekwe ase omogaso gose ekiriri ementwe omogaso buna egokina. Eekororekana buya ekero chibekire ase ekiriri akeigo. Ekero chiamete ase omogaso omogima, ekobi ekobwatana n’amato asitia ekara machani. Ebimeri bietaneti emiaka 3 nabo bikogachwa isiko y’egeticha ase omwaka omogima onye komenyete ase riberera ritari goetania chidigiri 10. Buna enkendu, epamu ekoremereria obokendu nigo etakeire gosimekwa ase riroba rieteti amache buya naende ebekwemaate. Omobisa omonene bw’epamu eye tari bokendu korende riroba ribwate amache amange. Ribererea riainse mono amo n’eriroba ribwate amache amange nigo agosaria emerio. Epamu eye nabo ekonyara komenyera obokendu chidigiri –15 goika –20. Riberera ria inse mono rimanyire yamenyerete riarenge chidigiri –28.
english: Rhapidophyllum hystrix Rhapidophyllum hystrix is a plant from the large palm family of the palm tree. The leaf is a typical leaf of the genus Rhapidophyllum. It originates from the forests of the southeastern United States. The seed is collected and planted so that about 20 seeds can be transported to Europe each year. It is also a fan palm, reaching a height of 1–3 meters with a trunk diameter of up to 17.8 cm. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix is a relatively easy-to-grow plant, its roots grow well in shady areas. On fertile soil, the roots become very large. The fan palm does not have climbing roots, but rather roots that reach a length of 1.2 m and a depth of 17.8 cm. The roots are brown, fibrous, and branched. They spread widely, forming a dense network. Once established, they can tolerate drought conditions. The leaves are arranged in a fan shape and are deeply divided. They are green in color and take about 3 years to mature. They are resistant to pests. The fan palm grows well in shade and can withstand cold temperatures. It reproduces through suckers. The fan palm usually grows in moist soils and can also grow in slightly acidic soils. It adapts well to different environments. Its growth rate depends on soil quality, moisture, and temperature. It takes about 3 years for the seedlings to develop a strong root system. However, the palm requires fertile soil to grow quickly and thrive. A healthy palm that is not stressed will produce more shoots. Cold tolerance varies depending on the variety, but most varieties can tolerate temperatures down to -15 to -20 degrees Celsius. Extremely low temperatures below -28 degrees Celsius can cause damage.

english: It will be good for those servants whose master finds them watching when he comes. I tell you the truth, he will dress himself to serve, will have them recline at the table and will come and wait on them.

ekegusii: Oyio noro omobaro bwe chiamate chi’Abakohati abwo baare konyara gokora emeremo agwo ase Eema y’Omosangererekano, abwo Musa na Haroni babarete, buna Omonene achigete Musa.
english: This was the total of all those in the Kohathite clans who served in the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the LORD's command through Moses.

ekegusii: Aye egetunwa ekenene, ninki oisaine ase obosio bwa Serubabeli? Noiranigwe inse obe buna ense omweya. Serubabeli nabeke rigena ri’ogokoorera, abanto kobaakire eriogi, bagoteba: Obuya, obuya bobe igoro yaye!”
english: "What are you, O mighty mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground. Then he will bring out the capstone to shouts of 'God bless it! God bless it!'"

ekegusii: Okogwa okwo nkobe buna ogwatwa kw’enyongo y’omokori chinyongo egotinerwa inse, nonya norogio oromo rw’enyongo eyio tirori gotoka omonto araancharere omorero, gose arabuchere amache korwa ase ensoko.”
english: It will break in pieces like pottery, shattered so mercilessly that among its pieces not a fragment will be found for taking coals from a hearth or scooping water out of a cistern."

ekegusii: amato aye arenge amaya, na amatunda aye namange, na ase omote oria endagera nao yarenge goisanekia abanto bonsi. Inse yaye ching’iti chi’orosana nao chiare konyora ekiriri chigokenderera, na ase chinsagia chiaye chinyoni chikaba chikomenyao.
english: with beautiful leaves and abundant fruit, providing food for all, giving shelter to the beasts of the field, and having nesting places in its branches for the birds of the air--

ekegusii: “Ase ayio Omonene, Nyasae oito, akabeka Ogi, omoruoti o Basani, amo nabanto baye bonsi, ase amaboko aito. Togaita bonsi pi, nonya noyomo tatigara ore moyo.
english: So the LORD our God also gave into our hands Og king of Bashan and all his army. We struck them down, leaving no survivors.

ekegusii: Nereri ase chinyasae chionsi chi’ebisaku biria chisokoro chiane chiasiretie kegima yanyarete gokonya abanto baye korwa ase okoboko kwane?
english: Who of all the gods of these nations that my fathers destroyed has been able to save his people from me? How then can your god deliver you from my hand?

ekegusii: Onye bagweitia na koonchoka ase ebirengererio biabo bionsi na ase chinkoro chiabo chionsi, ekero bare ase ense eria y’ababisa babo, baria baboosete, na aroro bagosabe barigereretie gochia ase ense yabo, eria kwaete chisokoro chiabo, na barigererie omochie oyo gwachorire na enyomba eye naagachire ase ogosasima erieta riao,
english: and if they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and pray to you toward the land you gave their fathers, toward the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your Name;

ekegusii: Risemi nigo rigokora omosacha oba nekeririanda, na takoba namabera ekero akorusia egesiomba.
english: for jealousy arouses a husband's fury, and he will show no mercy when he takes revenge.

ekegusii: Erio omonto ochenegete aimokie orosagia rwa hisopo, arotobeke ase amache ayio ime, erio anyororokerie eema na ebinto bionsi bireo, amo nabanto barenge imeo. Naende anyororokerie omonto oria okunete riuga, gose okunete omonto oitetwe, gose oyokwete bweka, gose oboina.
english: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water and sprinkle the tent and all the furnishings and the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who has touched a human bone or a grave or someone who has been killed or someone who has died a natural death.

ekegusii: Abanto nigo barenge koruera ebing’wanso ase ebisasimero biarenge aase aimokererete igoro, ekiagera nyomba ende yonsi konya teraagachwa ase baranyare gosasima erieta ri’Omonene.
english: The people, however, were still sacrificing at the high places, because a temple had not yet been built for the Name of the LORD.

ekegusii: Ekero bwakia mambia bagatiga abarwani be chibarasi bagenderere norogendo na Paulo, na barabwo abanyene bakairana ase enyomba enene y’abarwani.
english: The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.

ekegusii: Yoshua agatoma abanto korwa Yeriko gochia Ai, omochie ore moocha ya Beteli, ang’e na Beti‐Aveni, bagende baroote ense eria. Erio bagatiira kogenda koroota Ai.
english: Now Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth Aven to the east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and spy out the region." So the men went up and spied out Ai.

ekegusii: Inee! Ebibe biria twakorete ase ogosasima Peori tibiatoisanete? Korwa ase ebibe biria titwana gochenwa nonya ngoika rero iga, na egesusuro gekanyora omoganda bwonsi bw’Omonene.
english: Was not the sin of Peor enough for us? Up to this very day we have not cleansed ourselves from that sin, even though a plague fell on the community of the LORD!

ekegusii: Inche natachire bokong’u ase amabarato aye, nabeire ndendete chinchera chiaye, gose tindi koonchoka nchitige.
english: My feet have closely followed his steps; I have kept to his way without turning aside.

ekegusii: monyare koria na konywa ase emesa yane ase oboruoti bwane, na goikaransa ase ebirogo bi’obonene, na kogambia abanto b’ebisaku ikomi na bibere bi’Abaisraeli.”
english: so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

ekegusii: Ekero achia goika Yerusalemu agateema kobwatana naborokigwa; na barabwo bonsi bakamoiroka, ekiagera tibanchete ng’a ere nomworokigwa arenge.
english: When he came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he really was a disciple.

ekegusii: Endagera Sulemani arenge korenterwa ase rituko erimo nigo yarenge: obosie obonuke, ebitonga amagana atato, na obosie bonde, ebitonga amagana atano na rimo,
english: Solomon's daily provisions were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,

ekegusii: “Nonya Oholiba, mosubati omwaabo, oroche ayio, ere nigo abete omosareku goetania ase okoba nokogania okobe, na gokora obonyaka; obobe bwaye nigo bwabete obonge goetania obwa Ohola, mosubati omwabo.
english: "Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet in her lust and prostitution she was more depraved than her sister.

ekegusii: Abagaaka baria bakamoiraneria, “Korabe omwororo ase abanto aba na kobagwenera, naende okwane amang’ana amaya asebare, barabwo nababe bakogokorera botambe.”
english: They replied, "If you will be kind to these people and please them and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your servants."

ekegusii: Korende ase engaki eyio Hana tagendeteo, agatebia omosacha oye, “Ninganye goika ntache omwana, erio nario ndamoire imoorokie ase obosio bw’Omonene, erinde imotige amenye aroro botambe.”
english: Hannah did not go. She said to her husband, "After the boy is weaned, I will take him and present him before the LORD, and he will live there always."

ekegusii: Omonene agakwana na Musa, akamotebia,
english: The LORD said to Moses:

ekegusii: Naki onye ngwetogia asare ase engencho yaino, tinasoogetigwe; korende buna twabatebetie amang’ana onsi ase ekeene, naboigo nogwetogia gwaito ase obosio bwa Tito nigo kwarenge ogw’ekeene.
english: I had boasted to him about you, and you have not embarrassed me. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting about you to Titus has proved to be true as well.

ekegusii: Bono nigo ngoteba, “Onye ndiria nabwate chimbaba buna riruma, nanga nigo nare koiruruka ngende gotimoka.
english: I said, "Oh, that I had the wings of a dove! I would fly away and be at rest--

ekegusii: Ase ayio endamwamu y’Omonene ekaba enene ase ense eye, ere akarenta okoragereria gwonsi okwo korikire ase ebuku eye.
english: Therefore the LORD's anger burned against this land, so that he brought on it all the curses written in this book.

ekegusii: Aya nigo abanyorete, ekiagera ebibe biakorire ase omochie bw’abanto baane nigo biarenge ebinene kobua ebi’abanto ba Sodomu, omochie oyio nigo oonchoranetwe ase etagika eyemo, na okoboko kw’onde tikwayokunete.
english: The punishment of my people is greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment without a hand turned to help her.

ekegusii: “Kamorarende na kobwata amachiko ’Omonene, Nyasae oino, na gotaara ase chinchera chiaye, nabaimokererie igoro mobe abanto abachenu asare, buna abariereire eira na gotiana.
english: The LORD will establish you as his holy people, as he promised you on oath, if you keep the commands of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.

ekegusii: Ekeene, eng’eria nekare bosio, na ogosemeria kwao tikogosira bosa.
english: There is surely a future hope for you, and your hope will not be cut off.

ekegusii: Obuya bobe asemore na omorembe bikorwa ase Nyasae Tata oito, na ase Omonene Yeso Kristo.
english: Grace and peace to you from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

ekegusii: Akaonchora na ense ere entobu ekaba ekerubo ki’omonyo, ase engencho y’obobe bw’abanto bamenyeteo.
english: and fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of those who lived there.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, aye irana ase Nyasae oo. Obwatie obwanchani na oboronge, na obe komosemeretie Nyasae oo botambe.
english: But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and wait for your God always.

ekegusii: Nonya nekero ntarakwana ring’ana rinde rionsi, Naama, aye Omonene nigo orimanyete kegima.
english: Before a word is on my tongue you know it completely, O LORD.

ekegusii: akarandia noboremu ase erieta ri’Omonene. Agakwana na koamererania n’Abayahudi abarenge gokwana Ekegiriki, korende barabwo bakarigia komoita.
english: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.

ekegusii: “Aya naro Omonene Nyasae agoteba: Ninsirie emegwekano egosasimwa, ee, ninsirie kegima chinyasae chi’oborimo chia Memifisi, gose omogambi takoba ase ense ya Misiri; ase igo nindete obwoba ase ense eyio.
english: "'This is what the Sovereign LORD says: "'I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. No longer will there be a prince in Egypt, and I will spread fear throughout the land.

ekegusii: Buna anyororokeria amaguta aya ase omobere one, onkoreire aya ase okombeka ang’e ase ogotindekwa kwane.
english: When she poured this perfume on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

ekegusii: Na gatomanyete ng’a nigo agotoigwa ase kende gionsi togosaba, twamanyire ng’a twanyorire keria twasabire korwa asare.
english: And if we know that he hears us-- whatever we ask-- we know that we have what we asked of him.

ekegusii: “Boigo nasoe ase ense eria engiya, nasirie chinse chinyinge, korende Abaedomu na Abamoabu, na abanto abange b’Abaamoni, barabwo mbatoorigwe korwa ase okoboko kwaye.
english: He will also invade the Beautiful Land. Many countries will fall, but Edom, Moab and the leaders of Ammon will be delivered from his hand.

ekegusii: Inche ngateba: “Inwe abatang’ani b’abanto ba Yakobo, inwe abagambi b’Abaisraeli, igwa! Inee! Tebagwenereti inwe momanye ayare ay’oboronge?
english: Then I said, "Listen, you leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel. Should you not know justice,

ekegusii: Nigo akorora ng’a emeremo yaye nigo ekorenta ebitoki, na etaya yaye teri korima nyomba mwaye botuko.
english: She sees that her trading is profitable, and her lamp does not go out at night.

ekegusii: “Rirube mwatoma gocha asetore riasomirwe buya asende, nariigure.
english: The letter you sent us has been read and translated in my presence.

ekegusii: Abana abamura b’Onamu nabwo Samai na Yada. Abana abamura ba Samai nabwo Nadabu na Abisuri.
english: The sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.

ekegusii: Ebirengero bi’oborito, na ebi’obonge, bire ara kabere, nigo bire okogechia ase Omonene.
english: Differing weights and differing measures-- the LORD detests them both.

ekegusii: Kera omwaka akaba okogenda goika Beteli, na Giligali, na Misipa, akaba okogambera Abaisraeli ebina ase emechie eyio yonsi.
english: From year to year he went on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all those places.

ekegusii: Monto onde bwensi aise koroisia amanukato anga buna ayio ase okwegokeria rimisu riaye nigo araatananwe korwa ase egesaku ki’abanto b’Omonene.”
english: Whoever makes any like it to enjoy its fragrance must be cut off from his people."

ekegusii: Naende Abaisraeli bagakora amabe ase obosio bw’Omonene, na ase engencho y’ayio Omonene akabarentera Egiloni, omoruoti bw’ense ya Moabu, nere akabarwania, akababua.
english: Once again the Israelites did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and because they did this evil the LORD gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel.

ekegusii: Na endagera koyamire, bwango nigo akoira omoyio okogesa, ekiagera rigesa riaikire ang’e.”
english: As soon as the grain is ripe, he puts the sickle to it, because the harvest has come."

ekegusii: Egekondemia ase emechando yane neke: Ring’ana riao nigo rigonkora naba omoyia.
english: My comfort in my suffering is this: Your promise preserves my life.

ekegusii: Akarora omoko oyomo ase enchera ensemo, akayochiera, tarora gento asoro otatiga amato oka. Akayotebia, “Korwa bono tokwama amatunda nonya ndinde.” Erio kegima omoko oyio okoma.
english: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. Then he said to it, "May you never bear fruit again!" Immediately the tree withered.

ekegusii: Korwa ase Abaheburoni, Yeria nere otenenerete abanto be chiamate chionsi chi’ororeria rwa Heburoni. (Ase omwaka bw’emerongo ene bw’okogamba gwa Daudi, obotuki bogakorwa, na abanto be chiamate echio abamanyete korwana esegi buya bakanyorekana agwo Yaeseri ya Gileadi).
english: As for the Hebronites, Jeriah was their chief according to the genealogical records of their families. In the fortieth year of David's reign a search was made in the records, and capable men among the Hebronites were found at Jazer in Gilead.

ekegusii: Na ense ekamera bionsi ebigokina: ebimeri bikorua chimbusuro chiabo chinyene, na emete ekwama amatunda are ne chimbusuro chire imeo, kera oyomo ase egesaku kiaye ekenyene. Nyasae akarora ayio ng’a namaya.
english: The land produced vegetation: plants bearing seed according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed in it according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

ekegusii: Korende inche nigo intoereretie omoyo one; buna omwana otigire okogonka oagatire koboko kwa ng’ina, ee, naboigo omoyo one ore ime yane.
english: But I have stilled and quieted my soul; like a weaned child with its mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.

ekegusii: Korende onye timogotegerera, inche nindere bobisi ase engencho y’oboenenu bwaino. Nindere nobororo obonge, na amariga amange aiteke korwa ase amaiso aane, ekiagera riicho ri’Omonene rioosirwe na koirwa ase obosomba.
english: But if you do not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly, overflowing with tears, because the LORD's flock will be taken captive.

ekegusii: Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with him, and he with me.
english: Rigereria, ninteneine gesieri gotura; omonto karaigwe eriogi riane na koigora egesieri, ninsoe asare, nindagere amo nere, na ere amo nainche.

ekegusii: Bono nabatebirie, remia chinkoro chiaino, ekiagera monto tagosira, otatiga emeeri yoka.
english: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.

ekegusii: Korende bakamotebia amang’ana onsi Yusufu abatebetie. Ere agachia korora chigari chiria Yusufu amotomerete chigocha komoimokia, omoyo oye okaba nobogima oboyia.
english: But when they told him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the carts Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.

ekegusii: otatiga ase engencho ye ring’ana erimo natebete neriogi rinene, ekero natenenete egati yabo. Ngateba: Ase engencho y’okobokigwa kw’abakure nakio nkogamberigwa ase obosio bwaino iga rero.”
english: unless it was this one thing I shouted as I stood in their presence: 'It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.'"

ekegusii: Omonene onkorire nabeire ring’ana abanto bakorabaara, nabeire oyo abanto bagochaya ase ogotwa amate.
english: "God has made me a byword to everyone, a man in whose face people spit.

ekegusii: Nere otongete chinkoro chi’abanto bonsi, namanyete korenga ogokora kwabo gwonsi.
english: he who forms the hearts of all, who considers everything they do.

ekegusii: Ase ayio omorandia nigo agoteba. Aya mbosa, bosa; onsi mbosa kegima.
english: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"

ekegusii: Inyorokie ekemanyererio ki’obuya bwao, erinde abanto bangechete bakerore na gosookigwa, ekiagera aye Omonene gwankonyire na kondemia.
english: Give me a sign of your goodness, that my enemies may see it and be put to shame, for you, O LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

ekegusii: Na Nyasae Omobui nagosesenie, agokinie, na oroiboro rwao naromente robe omoganda omonene bw’ebisaku.
english: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and increase your numbers until you become a community of peoples.

ekegusii: Akabeka amaboko aye igoro asare, na ere akaramboka erio kegima, akamotogia Nyasae.
english: Then he put his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and praised God.

ekegusii: Abasacha bande bakabwatana nere, bakeegena, na ase abwo narengeo Dionuso, oyomo bw’ekegambero ki’Areopago, naende omokungu oyomo ore korokwa Damari, na abande amo nabarabwo.
english: A few men became followers of Paul and believed. Among them was Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus, also a woman named Damaris, and a number of others.

ekegusii: Ase rituko riria amang’ana aya nakwanwe ase Yerusalemu: “Aye Sayoni, toiroka; totiga amaboko ao abe amoro.
english: On that day they will say to Jerusalem, "Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your hands hang limp.

ekegusii: Akagenda, agatoma amang’ana gochia ase Yehosafati, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, agateba, “Omoruoti bw’Abamoabu bwangire konyigwera. Inee! Aye nogende amo nainche torwanie abanto ba Moabu?” Yehosafati akairaneria, “Ee, ningende amo naye, na abanto baane amo nabanto bao, ne chibarasi chiane amo ne chibarasi chiao.”
english: He also sent this message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?" "I will go with you," he replied. "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

ekegusii: Amang’ana onsi agokorwa nigo akorenta omoroso otanyare gokwaneka. Amaiso tari goisaneka naya akorora, na amato tari goisaneka naya akoigwa.
english: All things are wearisome, more than one can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear its fill of hearing.

ekegusii: Korende Yonathani taigwete ekero ise achigete abanto ase okobatiania ng’a tibaria kende. Ase ayio, akarambaria enyimbo yarenge koboko kwaye akayechobia ase eriana rire nobooke ime, akaribwata, akariria. Erio amaiso aye akarora buya.
english: But Jonathan had not heard that his father had bound the people with the oath, so he reached out the end of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it into the honeycomb. He raised his hand to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.

ekegusii: Chinguru chiane chionsi chiaerire, nasenyentekire, nigo nkona‐kweumia ase engencho y’obororo bw’enkoro yane.
english: I am feeble and utterly crushed; I groan in anguish of heart.

ekegusii: Egento nekemo gekobanyora bonsi, omonyene oboronge na omonyabibe, oyore omuya na ochenegete na oyo otachenegeti, oyo okorua ebing’wanso na oyo otari kobirua. Buna ekoba ase omonto omuya, naboigo ekoba nase omonyabibe; buna ekoba ase oria okoria eira y’ogotiana, naboigo ekoba nase oria otari koria eira y’ogotiana.
english: All share a common destiny-- the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good man, so with the sinner; as it is with those who take oaths, so with those who are afraid to take them.

ekegusii: agateba, “Omonene, Nyasae bw’omonene one Ibrahimu, atogigwe! Ere tatigeti koorokia omonene one obuya na obwegenwa. Omonene ondaaire enchera, naikire enka y’abamwabo omonene one.”
english: saying, "Praise be to the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned his kindness and faithfulness to my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master's relatives."

ekegusii: "Suppose he has a violent son, who sheds blood or does any of these other things
english: “Ande omonto oyio nabe ng’a oiboire omwana omomura oyore omoibi na omoiti, gose abe ogokora erimo ri’ayio

ekegusii: mwanchare omorero mobekeo, na igoro y’omorero oyio mobeke ubani, naende mochirente ase obosio bw’Omonene. Omonto oria Omonene arachore, nere oyio orabe oria omochenu. Inwe Abalawi, bono ayio abaisanire.”
english: and tomorrow put fire and incense in them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. You Levites have gone too far!"

ekegusii: “Timoichana ase chinkoro chiaino; momwegene Nyasae, nainche monyegene.
english: "Do not let your hearts be troubled. Trust in God; trust also in me.

ekegusii: Amang’ana aya naro Lemweli omoruoti orokereretigwe na ng’ina:
english: The sayings of King Lemuel-- an oracle his mother taught him:

ekegusii: Omonene akabairaneria, “Inee! Tinabatooretie korwa ase Abamisiri, na Abaamori, na Abafilisti?
english: The LORD replied, "When the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines,

ekegusii: “Aye mwanyabanto, eroiserie chinchera ibere chikworokia ase omoro bw’omoruoti o Babeli oraetere. Echio ibere nigo chirarwe ase ense eyemo. Naende otenenie ekemanyererio ase amatabekania ’omochie.
english: "Son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to take, both starting from the same country. Make a signpost where the road branches off to the city.

ekegusii: Barabwo babe bagoisaba amaboko, basibie na amagoro, tibabaisa gokwa. Ayio nigo arabe ogochika koragenderere asare na ase ororeria rwaye ebiaare ase ebiaare.”
english: they shall wash their hands and feet so that they will not die. This is to be a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come."

Kiabeire kegotamburigwa bobe buna ekere Parajubaea tirali goika bwanko iga ekero okorigarigia gwakorwa okamanya korokwa Parajubaea sunkha. Chipamu echi chia Parajubaea nigo chigosimekwa raisi. Chintetere cnhire chigochaka komera magega y’omotienyi korense cnhire chikoira egeka egetambe goika omwaka gose emiaka ebere. Chintetere chirwete ase amatunda amanene goika chibekwe amache ase chiwiki ibere. Amache ayio aonchorwe kera rituko. Chintetere nabo chigosigikigwa nario chiremere bwanko. Okobeka chintetere amache ime nigo kogokora obworo bw’okomera, kobe buna nokorenta embura, ere enguya ase okomera. Obworo obwo ebokogera nchintetere nchikomera ekero ki’obokendu ase Bolivia (obokendu obonene bw’omotienyi ogatano na rimo amo n’omotienyi o gatano na kabere). Okomera okuya nigo gokorenta n’etobauti ase ribera mogaso (igoro) na botuko (inse). Ekero chintetere chiabusuiru, tichibasi kona kobekerwa amache rioka rioka ekiagere arachisari ekero ebimeri bire ebike. Ogosimaka ebimeri bia Parajubaea nigo kore etobauti n’ebimeri binde ekiagera otagete riberera rike amo na amache amake. Stop watering the seeds and let the soil dry out for few months. Take the seeds out of the soil, put them back into water for around a week and then sown them again. Otige konya koumora amache na oige riroba rioma ase emetieni mekeigo. Rusia chintetere oas riroba, chibeke ase amache ang’e echuma eyemo naende chioiranie ase riroba. Chintetere chisimekire igo echigwenererett komera ekero omwaka oyomo n’enusi oerire. Onye ntetere chinde cnhikomera, irora ne chintetere chionsi nchimere ekero embura egotwa naende. Okwamera kwa Parajubaea nigo kogoikerana 100%, kogincha omonto abe omoremereria, ae chintetere chiri ching’oro enkaki yokorakera. Ekero obwate e pamu enke, nigo ekoba enyomo pa, inyora tonyeumorera amache amange moono. Epamu enke nigo egotaka ase are gati gati (ekero chisimekire ase chiachakerete, nigo chogosimekwa ase ekiriri gi’echipamu chinene), korende chiri chinene echigotaka omogaso. Parajubaea nigo ere egesaku giepamu giaisire gosira pi ime ya America ya maate. Esababu enene ekogera nesengencho emete ekonachwa korigia amaremo yogosimeka endagera, korugia chibao nma korisia chiombe. Chipamu echi echigotika ase ake mono, naki chigosarerigwa bwanko igo chiaisire gosire pi. Ekiagera chintetere chiabo chire chinene, okwama ase aange nkori konyarekana. Eng’iti yorosana enene ekoira chintetere echi isiko y’ase echigotoka n’ebea ekorokwa naende (Tremarctos ornatus), korende neero negosire ase engencho abanto ebagochiseri gose gochiita. ««« Previous article: Welwitschia mirabilis - ogosimeka kw’e obotobu bomenyete Next article: Omogati bw’amatunda Artocarpus odoratissimus, Marang »»»
english: Parajubaea torallyi grows natively in the moist forests of South America. Currently, it is cultivated as an ornamental tree and in arboretums, Bolivia being its main center of interest due to its large population, which is threatened by deforestation. Found in Bolivia, it grows at altitudes between 2700–3400 meters above sea level in the Inter-Andean dry forest; however, some populations grow at lower altitudes in more humid environments. It flowers after about 20 years and has a trunk diameter of up to 1 meter. It can reach heights of up to 7 meters in cultivation (with a crown spread of 5 to 8 meters) and lives for approximately 550 years. It needs well-drained soil to thrive, prefers full sun, a trunk, and also requires adequate drainage to prevent root rot, benefiting people who want to plant it because it is easy to grow. Large trunks become hollow and those associated with old age are prone to decay, making them unsuitable for use as timber. It is said that in Europe, trunks can reach diameters of 3 meters. The palm thrives in areas where temperatures rarely drop below -8 degrees Celsius. Many birds feed on its fruits, but they remain mostly in the highlands, beautiful palms! In Bolivia, the palm grows to a height of 14 meters with a trunk diameter of 25–35 centimeters. The palm can live for 100 years and reach a height of 30 meters with a trunk diameter of 50 centimeters. Some individuals have been reported to reach heights of 20 meters! The trees are common in the cloud forests of Bolivia. It is a relatively fast-growing palm, but it does not grow as quickly as other species due to its size. This species is classified as P. torallyi var. microcarpa with smaller leaves and P. torallyi var. torallyi with larger leaves. However, there is confusion, var. microcarpa tends to grow more slowly, while those in drier and warmer climates grow faster. Its conservation status is considered vulnerable due to habitat loss. Nevertheless, its seeds germinate easily, provided they are fresh and kept moist, and planted shallowly. Well-maintained plants, with adequate watering and fertilization, benefit greatly from this care, especially during the first few years, and the seedlings will be strong and healthy. It needs regular care, including pruning, fertilizing, and protecting against pests and diseases, benefiting people who appreciate this native tree and also helping to conserve the species and its habitat. Parajubaea torallyi and its relatives are important ecologically and economically. In Ecuador and Colombia, Parajubaea cocoides grows at altitudes between 2500–3000 meters – the palm is found on slopes and is not very common. It is closely related to Parajubaea torallyi, and sometimes confused with other species of Parajubaea torali. Other populations were discovered in Peru in the 1990s, identified as Parajubaea sunkha which is similar and was described in 1996. It grows up to 8 meters tall and is found in the Andean foothills near Vallegrande in the Santa Cruz region of Bolivia at elevations between 1700–2200 meters. There has been some confusion about whether Parajubaea tirali is the same as Parajubaea sunkha. The seed of Parajubaea germinates easily. The fruit is used locally for food. Those interested should collect the fruits, but they need to be cleaned well and sown fresh, and they need moisture throughout the year. The seeds sprout readily when kept moist for several months. Old seeds may take longer to germinate. Flowering occurs annually, producing abundant flowers. The flowering period lasts for several months each year. Typically, the seeds collected from the fruit are approximately 20 mm long and 5–7 mm wide. The seeds are covered with a hard shell. The shells are often cracked during collection. The seeds also require stratification before sowing. To germinate the seeds, it's necessary to simulate the conditions of the rainy season (wet and dry periods), mimicking the environment where they grow (especially in Bolivia - areas with distinct wet and dry seasons). After cracking the shells, the seeds that have been collected should be soaked in water for several weeks, alternating between soaking and drying. Stop watering the seeds and let the soil dry out for few months. Take the seeds out of the soil, put them back into water for around a week and then sown them again. Don't delay planting the seeds and provide adequate moisture. Soak the seeds first, then place them in damp cloth and sow them. The seedlings take about a year to mature and produce leaves. Any damaged seedlings, discard them along with those that don't sprout after being watered. The germination rate of Parajubaea can reach 100%, producing strong sprouts, and the seeds are very resistant to damage. In some cases, there may be a small hole, which indicates good viability; otherwise, the seed will not germinate unless it's fully intact. A large hole indicates a better chance of sprouting. Parajubaea is native to isolated areas of eastern South America. A major reason for its decline is deforestation due to agriculture, leading to habitat loss and fragmentation. The palm tree that grows here is unique and rare. Larger seeds are more likely to survive. The growth of these seeds is affected by animals like the spectacled bear (Tremarctos ornatus), which disperse the seeds across wider areas. ««« Previous article: Welwitschia mirabilis - a plant from the Namib desert Next article: Omogati bw’amatunda Artocarpus odoratissimus, Marang »»»
